rounds.text: Viceroy Hotels Ltd is demonstrating powerful underlying commercial momentum, highlighted by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 33% and trailing twelve month sales growth of 24% [E9, E11]. Profitability is scaling alongside top-line expansion, evidenced by an operating margin reaching 28% in the TTM against 13% three years prior, and a yearly operating-margin trend that has been increasing over the last six years [E21, E23]. This operational progress is paired with supreme management alignment, as promoters dramatically increased their stake to 84.11% in Jun 2026 from 13.41% in Sep 2023 [E32]. Furthermore, the business is benefiting from a strong Consumer Services sector tailwind score of +0.84, while the intrinsic valuation derived from discounted cash flows sits above the current market price of ₹ 125, offering a margin of safety [E35, E63]. Viceroy Hotels Ltd carries significant valuation and operational risks that are masked by short-term metrics, starting with a lofty valuation at a P/E of 36.8x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 3.16x [E2]. The underlying return profile is decidedly weak, delivering an ROCE of just 7.1% [E6] and an ROE of 7.2% [E7], both sitting below sector medians [E68]. Compounding this poor efficiency, the company exhibits severe cash burn with a free cash flow of Rs -65 Cr in March 2026 [E27], driven by a sudden ballooning of borrowings to Rs 264 Cr from Rs 52 Cr the prior year [E30]. Furthermore, momentum is entirely absent as the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40], accompanied by a dismal relative-strength rating of 34 against the Nifty 500 [E41], an annualised volatility of 64.1% [E44], and a Sharpe ratio of merely 0.04 [E45]. Conceded: the company displays robust 5-year and TTM sales growth [E9, E11], significant margin expansion [E21], and strong operating cash flow backed fully by profits in March 2026 [E25, E26].

Even so, the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a weak relative-strength rating of 34, a brutal historical drawdown of -99.7%, high volatility of 64.1%, and a negligible Sharpe ratio of 0.04 [E40, E41, E43, E44, E45].
